source.check: candidates, labels, electorate, valid votes and majority from the News-Letter's ward-by-ward results (INA OCR); * = retiring member as printed; where the OCR of a vote is garbled the figure used is the one that agrees with both the printed valid votes and the printed majority; full names from the nomination list

note: Annual election of one councillor in each of the 15 wards of Belfast Corporation (the member retiring in rotation), nominations Saturday 5 January, poll Tuesday 15 January 1924. Ten wards were contested; Falls, St Anne's, Shankill, Smithfield and Windsor returned their members unopposed (Belfast News-Letter, 7 and 16 January 1924). Labour gained Court and Dock, and an Independent Unionist St George's. Stewart's vote reads 6,529 in the OCR; 5,529 agrees with the printed valid votes (8,920) and majority (2,138). The leader on page 7 gives the majority as 2,158. Lynn, the retiring member, stood as the Town Tenants' Association candidate.
